description:
RFC 8621 §4.2 (Email/get) and §4.9 (Email/parse) define the wire field as
`fetchHTMLBodyValues` — *HTML* in uppercase. See rfc8621.txt lines 2327, 2438,
3163.

Current code (`src/methods/mod.rs:50` for EmailGetParams.fetch_html_body_values,
plus same in EmailParseParams at line ~267) uses
`#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` which produces `fetchHtmlBodyValues`
(lowercase html). Inline test at mod.rs:665 even asserts the wrong wire
spelling: `assert_eq!(v["fetchHtmlBodyValues"], json!(false));`.

Impact: a spec-strict server treats the field as unknown (RFC 8620 §3.6.3
for unknown invocation arguments; usually silently ignored for unknown
body-fetch hints), HTML body values are NEVER inlined, and the client
silently gets empty htmlBody bodyValues for every Email/get and Email/parse
call the caller asked for HTML inlining. Caller sees no error.

This is the kind of bug that survives indefinitely because misalignment is
silent and the deserializer is happy with the resulting empty bodyValues map.

Fix: add `#[serde(rename = "fetchHTMLBodyValues")]` to the
`fetch_html_body_values` field on both EmailGetParams and EmailParseParams.
Update the inline test oracle to the correct wire spelling.

This bug is the canonical-template kind: every extension-client sibling will
have been cookie-cut from the same shape. Audit chat/calendars/tasks/contacts/
filenode/sharing/metadata clients for the same misspelling pattern when fixing.
title: EmailGetParams/EmailParseParams: fetchHtmlBodyValues vs RFC fetchHTMLBodyValues (HTML uppercase)
